judy: morning — nightly perf job flagged a latency regression (~12%) on our FFN-heavy workloads at seq=4096/8192. profiler points at a Triton kernel choice flip during step 2 of ffn_forward. perf-bot: <@judy> detected: nightly/ffn-latency ↑12% (compare: 2103370000 -> 2103450000). link: https://ci.internal/redwood/perf/2103456789 :rotating_light:
liam: can you paste the flamegraph slice or nvprof output? curious if it's launch/config vs algo selection. :eyes:
judy: pasted low-noise snippet from nvprof (reduced):
```
# nvprof trace
ffn_kernel_triton: 82.3ms (chosen)
ffn_kernel_cublaslt: 45.1ms (compatible)
alloc_workspace: 310MiB -> failed fallback to slab-reclaim
KV-pad reserve: increased from 48MiB -> 128MiB for seq=8192
```

natalie: hmm KV padding growth explains workspace pressure. when Triton kernel probes it requires contiguous workspace > cublaslt path so allocator picks slab->evict->probe and we hit slow path. we recently changed kv_cache_reserve to be per-request instead of per-session (PR #1421) — may have multiplied worst-case contiguous requirement.
ben: this rings true. Triton FFN variants use temp tensor tiled layout which wants big contiguous chunk (temp_fp16 activations + partials). cuBLASLt streams smaller GEMM buffers so less single-chunk pressure.
liam: can we force a heuristic: if contiguous_free < threshold then prefer cuBLASLt kernel? quick guard before heavy refactor.
judy: I sketched a patch: set kernel_prefer_order: [cuBLASLt, Triton] when (seq >= 4096 and kv_pad > 64MiB and batch <= 4). config snippet: `kernel_selector.overrides.large_seq_kv = cublaslt_first`
ben: sounds fine. also add metric to detect kernel-choice flip on hot path so we can rollback automatically if latency spikes.
perf-bot: telemetry suggestion: emit `kernel_choice_reason` tag on every ffn request (values: default, mem_guard, perf_hint, user_override) and a histogram of workspace_alloc_peak.
judy: ran a quick canary locally with `kernel_selector.overrides.large_seq_kv=cublaslt_first` — results: median latency down 9%, p95 down 13% on seq=8192 microbench, allocator logs show avoided slab-evict.
natalie: good. couple follow-ups: 1) update allocator to expose contiguous_free() cheaply, 2) ensure kv_cache padding strategy can be bounded by session-level cap, 3) add unit test that simulates probe path with small batch + large seq.
liam: won't forget telemetry. I'll open an alert rule: if kernel_choice flips to Triton on large-seq workloads AND p50 increases >5% for 30m, auto-fallback to previous selector.
ben: can we also try transient buffer reuse: keep a small pool of pre-reserved contiguous chunks for Triton probes (LRU) to avoid repeated eviction thrash? might reduce tail latency but cost memory. tradeoff.
judy: agree — for now prefer cheaper guard (selector override + telemetry) then iterate with a reserved-pool experiment. I'll open PR for selector change + tests. assigning to @ben for reserved-pool design and @natalie for allocator change.
liam: thanks — add the perf job id to the PR description so CI can re-run nightly regression check.
judy: created issue and PR draft: https://git.internal/rw/infra/merge/2387 — notes + before/after microbench numbers attached. planning canary on dedicated pool tomorrow. :thumbsup:
ben: ack, will prototype pool and post mem/latency tradeoffs in the thread.
perf-bot: closing comment: set milestone to 2.8.1-hotfix if canary confirms.
